projects.title: ADHD Project Manager
projects.hook: A scheduled scan that catches everything I leave midway across AI chats and lands it on one prioritized board. Built for my ADHD; built so anyone can repurpose it.

body.problem: AI chats are where work goes to die midway — brilliant threads abandoned, commitments unconfirmed, and no single place to see what's actually open.
body.approach: A scheduled scan reads every thread, finds open loops, and lands them on one prioritized board: sense → draft → queue → review.
body.hers: Designed from my own failure modes — ADHD as a design constraint, never an apology. Produced is not shipped.
body.result: One board, every open loop, ranked. The scan runs daily; I clear it in one sitting.
body.lesson: The job isn't organizing tasks. It's noticing them.

projects.title: The CMS behind this site
projects.hook: My portfolio runs on plain HTML and JSON — and I edit every word of it from a custom admin panel, no developer needed.
projects.visualAlt: Diagram: admin panel edits JSON, GitHub API commits, three sites go live

body.problem: Static sites are cheap and fast, but every copy change meant editing HTML by hand — or paying for a CMS I didn't need. I wanted blog-style editing with flat-file simplicity.
body.approach: Built a single-page admin that reads and writes the sites' JSON content files through the GitHub API. Edit words, upload photos, reorder sections, hit save — live in about a minute. No build step, no database, no monthly bill.
body.hers: Designed from my own failure modes — I kept breaking things with half-finished edits, so every section saves independently and the editor links straight to the page it changes.
body.result: One admin runs all three of my sites. Every word on the About page was edited there.
body.lesson: The best tool is the one you'll actually use.

prototyping: More tools are in the workshop — each one earns its card here when it has a live demo and a written playbook.
